title: Slot-oriented KV slab rotation and GPU residency protocol
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Goal: Design and implement a slot-oriented paged/blocked KV cache allocator and GPU residency protocol that reduces OOMs and tail latency under oversubscription, while preserving continuous-batching throughput. Scope includes allocator layout, residency tracking, async reclamation protocol, prefetch and batching hints, and runtime knobs for saturation/thermal behavior.

Background: We currently use a variable-size block allocator for KV entries. Under high-concurrency and diverse sequence-length workloads we observe fragmentation, frequent GPU-to-host swaps, and batch tail spikes. Existing proposals in the backlog are fragmented (slab/paged variants) and duplicate eviction heuristics. This ticket consolidates a single implementation variant that focuses on fixed slot slabs, time-ordered rotation, and a lightweight residency protocol optimized for continuous batching.

Design summary:
- Physical layout: per-GPU slab composed of fixed-size slots (32KB base slot with configurable slot multipliers), grouped into buckets by slot-size class. Each slab exposes a residency bitmap and a generation counter per slot.
- Allocation policy: fast path allocates from free-bit run using atomic bit-scans; slow path triggers slot rotation where the oldest generation slots are soft-marked for reclamation. Soft-marked slots remain readable to ongoing batches until async reclamation completes.
- Residency protocol: keep a GPU-resident bitmap (bitmap mirrored on host for quick scans) and a small LRU-ish ring of recently-used slot indices to bias eviction away from hot prefixes. The runtime maintains a resident_ratio metric and an eviction_score per slot based on recency + prefix-heatmap weight.
- Eviction/reclamation: two-phase: 1) soft-mark (publish generation++ and set soft-evict flag) so new continuous batches avoid selecting the slot for prefetch; 2) background reclaim worker streams remaining data out (if dirty) and atomically clears the slot. Reclamation is limited per-interval to respect latency SLOs.
- Prefetch hints: continuous-batching controller emits per-batch prefetch candidates (slot indices or bucket IDs) based on prefix-KV hits and store-level frequency counts. Prefetch worker issues async GPU copies and updates the residency bitmap.
- GPU paging behavior: when resident_ratio falls below configurable thresholds, fallback policies engage: (a) prefer CPU-hosted page with async copy on first use; (b) opportunistic compaction across slabs to reduce fragmentation; (c) if thermal/oom risk detected, throttle batch coalescing and raise a backpressure signal to the serving layer.
- Integration with batching: batch scheduler prefers requests whose KV candidates are resident to reduce per-token kernel latency. Batches with mixed residency get served with prioritized ordering to minimize tail.

Trade-offs considered: fixed-size slots simplify fragmentation but can increase internal waste for very small KV entries — mitigated via multiple slot classes. Soft-marking avoids blocking in-flight batches at the cost of delayed reclamation. Mirroring small bitmaps to host increases CPU work but enables faster eviction scoring without heavy device queries.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation passes microbench suite (resident_ratio, eviction_rate, reclaim_latency, avg_kernel_latency) and shows >=30% reduction in GPU-host swap count under the oversubscription synthetic workload compared to baseline.
- No increase in 95th percentile batch-tail latency beyond target (5ms) in mixed-residency workloads.
- Feature flags to toggle slot size classes and reclamation window exist and documented.
- End-to-end canary deployment on dedicated pool with telemetry dashboards (resident_ratio, eviction_score_distribution, reclaimed_bytes_per_min).
